title: Kyrgyz — passport-style ASCII (observed practice)
authority: No published table; Cabinet Resolution No. 651 of 29 Sept 2026 lets applicants choose their Latin spelling
description: Kyrgyz Cyrillic names in the ASCII form common in Kyrgyz passports: Ң→N, Ө→O, Ү→U, Ж→ZH, Х→KH, initial and post-vowel Е→YE, Ю/Я→YU/YA, final Й→Y, Ь/Ъ dropped (Атамбаев → Atambayev, Жуманазарова → Zhumanazarova, Тыныбекова → Tynybekova).
notes: Resolution No. 651 (29 Sept 2026, in force 10 days after publication) lets a citizen state the desired Latin spelling of surname, name and patronymic, provided meaning and phonetics are kept. Passport spellings therefore vary by holder; this scheme is only the most common default.
Earlier reporting (2015) found ж, к, ң, ы, ө, ү typed in 3–4 arbitrary variants (Жумагулов → Dzhumagulov, Хамид → Khamid vs Hamid). No official table was found; status informal.

Ж→ZH matches athletes' passport names (Meerim Zhumanazarova, Akzhol Makhmudov); politicians' official English forms use J (Sadyr Japarov, Sooronbay Jeenbekov). Generate J, DZH, ZH; also Ң→NG, Ө→OE/U, Ү→UE/YU, Ы→I, Е→E, Ю/Я→IU/IA (strict ICAO).
Patronymic markers уулу / кызы come out as uulu / kyzy.
